div.head: Leis Wl 2.2a
div.ab: E les forfez le rei, ki aferent al vescunte, L souz en Merchenelahe [e] XL souz en Westsexenelahe.
E lez forvaiz le roi, qui afierent al vescunte, XL solz en Merchenelae e L solz en Westsexelae.
[2,2a] Et forisfactum regis, quod ad uicecomitem pertinet, scilicet XL solid. in Merchenelahe et L solid. in Westsaxenelahe.
E les forfez le rei ki aferent al vescunte, XL souz en Merchenelahe e L souz en Westsexenelahe.
2, 2a. Und jene Königsverbrechen [öffentliche Bussen], welche dem Sheriff gehören: 40 Schill. im Mercier-Rechtsgebiet, 50 Schill. im Westsachsen-Rechtsgebiet.
2, 2a. And those royal crimes [public compensations] which belong to the sheriff: 40 shill. in the Mercian legal district, 50 shill. in the West Saxon legal district.
And [he who violates it in Mercia or Wessex shall pay] the king's fines which belong to the sheriff—40 shillings in the province of Mercia and 50 shillings in the province of Wessex.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 252–253 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text and German translation added from Gesetze I p. 493–495, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: In Agsächs. Zeit hiessen 480 Pfennig in Mercien und 600 in Wessex (= 40 bzw. 50 Schill. Normannisch) beide 120 Schilling, d. i. das Strafgeldfixum für Ungehorsam; s. d. Gl 4. 5. Im Mercischen Chester kennt dieses Strafgeldfixum (s. d. Gl 14) von 40 Schilling Domesdaybuch

In Anglo-Saxon times 480 pence in Mercia and 600 in Wessex (= 40 and 50 shill. Norman respectively) were both called 120 shillings, i.e. the fixed fine for disobedience; see that word in Gl 4. 5. Domesday Book knows this fixed fine (see that word in Gl 14) of 40 shillings in Mercian Chester
